title: The sheaf associated to a quasi-coherent module is quasi-coherent on the big and on the small site
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: For a quasi-coherent module F on a scheme S and a topology among Zariski, etale, smooth, syntomic and fppf, the lemma has two parts: the sheaf F^a is a quasi-coherent module on the big site of S, and for the Zariski and etale topologies it is quasi-coherent on the small site as well (statement lines 2615-2630). The proof is a complete localisation argument rather than a citation: it first records that quasi-coherence of F on the ringed space S produces a Zariski covering of S over which F admits a presentation by direct sums of the structure sheaf (proof lines 2633-2641), and then observes that the same presentation survives the passage to the site, either the big site or the small etale site, so that the local criterion for quasi-coherence applies (proof lines 2644-2656 and 2659-2670). The small Zariski case is then dismissed as tautological because the corresponding ringed topoi agree (proof lines 2671-2672). The claim is H2: the argument is short but it is a real reduction -- a presentation is produced, transported along the comparison of sites, and fed into a locality criterion -- and nothing in it is a restatement of the conclusion.
